inspiration.observed_pattern: A DELETE selects target IDs through nested derived subqueries, compares a grouped flagged-child count with a correlated total-child count through HAVING, and then removes only parents whose children all satisfy the flagged condition.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored customer-note purge. Nested derived tables make the target-table read safe during DELETE; only accounts whose complete note history is flagged are removed, while mixed, normal-only, and childless accounts remain.

fixture_notes: Account 801 has only flagged notes and is deleted; account 802 has flagged and normal notes and remains; account 803 has no notes and account 804 has only a normal note, so neither is selected.
determinism_notes: Account and note IDs are fixed, each grouped account has a stable primary key, and the final read orders by account ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE purge_accounts (account_id INT PRIMARY KEY, account_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE purge_notes (note_id INT PRIMARY KEY, account_id INT NOT NULL, note_state VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, note_text VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: DELETE FROM purge_accounts WHERE account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM (SELECT a.account_id, COUNT(n.note_id) AS flagged_notes, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM purge_notes AS all_notes WHERE all_notes.account_id = a.account_id) AS total_notes FROM purge_accounts AS a, purge_notes AS n WHERE n.account_id = a.account_id AND n.note_state = 'flagged' GROUP BY a.account_id HAVING flagged_notes = total_notes) AS all_flagged_accounts)

checks.sql: SELECT account_id, account_name FROM purge_accounts ORDER BY account_id
SELECT note_id, account_id, note_state FROM purge_notes ORDER BY note_id
